facts.raw_span: sickle cell disease (HbSS variant)
2-day history of visual loss in the left eye
No dehydration or other precipitating factors were noted
Visual acuity was 20/20 OD and 20/800 OS
peripheral retinal black sunburst lesions
ischemic macular whitening was noted
No cherry-red spot, hemorrhage, or peripheral neovascularization was present
abnormal retinal capillary bed across the macula, with increased intercapillary spacing and small areas of hypofluorescence nasal to the fovea
Hyperreflective plaques at the level of the INL/OPL, corresponding to ophthalmoscopically opaque areas
Temporal macular thinning

concepts.why: The patient has sickle cell disease and presents with retinal findings consistent with sickle cell retinopathy, including peripheral retinal black sunburst lesions and abnormal retinal capillary bed.
The patient presents with sudden visual loss in one eye, which is consistent with central retinal artery occlusion, and the presence of ischemic macular whitening supports this diagnosis.

The patient has sickle cell disease and presents with macular findings consistent with sickle cell maculopathy, including abnormal retinal capillary bed and hyperreflective plaques at the level of the INL/OPL.

rationales.F01: Sickle cell disease is a known risk factor for sickle cell retinopathy and maculopathy.
rationales.F04: Visual acuity loss is a common symptom of both central retinal artery occlusion and sickle cell maculopathy.
rationales.F05: Peripheral retinal black sunburst lesions are characteristic of sickle cell retinopathy.
rationales.F06: Ischemic macular whitening is a sign of retinal ischemia, which can occur in both central retinal artery occlusion and sickle cell maculopathy.
rationales.F08: Abnormal retinal capillary bed and increased intercapillary spacing are characteristic of sickle cell retinopathy and maculopathy.
rationales.F09: Hyperreflective plaques at the level of the INL/OPL are a sign of retinal damage, which can occur in sickle cell retinopathy and maculopathy.

frontier_selector.rationale: The patient's presentation of ischemic macular whitening, abnormal retinal capillary bed, and hyperreflective plaques at the level of the INL/OPL, along with the presence of sickle cell disease (HbSS variant), supports Sickle Cell Maculopathy as the most specific diagnosis.
